_comment: Reviewed, pragmatic exceptions to the architecture rule that nightshade_core is the only Dart package allowed to import package:nightshade_bridge (docs/architecture.md §1). Each entry needs a one-line reason AND a 'todo' marker ('TODO: relocate behind core seam') so the later cleanup pass can shrink this whitelist file-by-file. Two kinds qualify today: (1) the desktop headless appliance layer, which IS the local hardware owner on the appliance (the FfiBackend-equivalent at the network seam, architecture §4-5) and legitimately drives Rust directly rather than going back through a network backend; (2) thin UI files that only need a bridge *data type* (an enum/struct) for display, where re-modeling the type in core would be churn for no behavioral benefit. UI files that call bridge *functions* (image processing, stretch, PHD2 control) are NOT whitelisted - those are real boundary leaks and must move behind a nightshade_core role. The audit loader reads only the 'file' and 'reason' keys; 'todo' is an in-data marker for human reviewers. See docs/production-readiness/bridge-boundary-plan.md.
